gen-dafont-quantum-gf-savate: Quantum draws plain, unshaded lines with loose spacing. Savate follows in a sans with sturdy hairlines and open jaws, its tall round o swelling slightly, so paragraphs move along smoothly.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Slick and wiry, Quantum glides under the eye with compressed ascenders and generous spacing between letters. Schibsted Grotesk gives it a friendly, wide-mouthed counterweight.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-sen: Sen is a tall-lowercase sans whose constant line stops short before curling inward, giving it a modern, unfussy feel. Sen against Quantum's loose, open-mouthed display letters makes the pair's strongest quality a shared lightness.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-sintony: Quantum sets loose, open letters with compressed ascenders. Sintony's chunky, tall midzone is the pair's strongest quality, a sturdy sans-serif smoothness that keeps curves from clogging beneath the heading's thin arches.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-sofia-sans: Quantum's arches carry the same thickness as its stems, with loose spacing and compressed ascenders. Sofia Sans stands its lowercase tall like cut acrylic, with no thick-thin modulation, so a long read stays crisp and steady.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-sono: Sono is a sans-serif with tall lowercase, wide default spacing and each a left ajar, which gives text a generous stride. Quantum's horizontals match its verticals, so headings and text feel cut from related stock.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-stack-sans-notch: Stack Sans Notch is a sans-serif with rod-stock strokes, open curves you can look right into, and big-bodied lowercase. Stack Sans Notch and Quantum share loose, open-mouthed lettering, which is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-stack-sans-text: Marker-like in its constant line, with curve endings held well apart and big-bodied lowercase, this sans feels plainly modern. Stack Sans Text does the sustained reading, while Quantum's loose, compressed display letters handle the attention-getting.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-sulphur-point: Quantum keeps its letters loose and its ascenders compressed. Quantum is best at crisp display lines, while Sulphur Point's bulky lowercase and open gaps in c, e, s and a carry the sustained reading in a steady sans.
